newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court widens public access to Commission documents.
newsitem.headline: Court widens public access to Commission documents.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance told the European Commission on Wednesday it cannot deny the public access to information based solely on a general need for confidentiality.
Although legitimate exceptions to the public's right to documents do exist, the court made it clear the Commission would have to detail its reasoning for withholding information.
The court distinguished two categories of exceptions to the general principle of the public's right of access to Commission documents.
The first exception obliged the Commission to deny access to information that would harm third parties' or the general public's interest.

In the second category, the only interest at stake is the internal deliberation of the institution. "The confidentiality which the member states were entitled to expect of the Commission warrants...a refusal of access to documents relating to investigations which might lead to an infringement procedure, the court said.

But the court said the Commission cannot justify refusal to documents solely on the basis of possible infringement proceedings, and must indicate why the documents in question would be needed for such a proceeding.
The court also noted that in adopting the Code of Conduct on public access to documents, the court said the Commission conferred legal rights on third parties.
The WWF took the Commission to the European Court of First Instance to force them to reveal information used in deciding not to fund a national park project in Western Ireland.
"This is an important victory for all who want to see more openness in European decision-making," said Tony Long, director of WWF's European Policy Office in Brussels.
A Commission spokesman said the Commission would analyze the decision over the next few weeks and decide whether to appeal the ruling to the European Court of Justice.
John Carvel of the Guardian won a similar case against the European Council in 1995.

application for the annulment of the Commission decision of 2 February 1995 refusing the applicant access to Commission documents relating to the examination of a project to build an interpretative centre at Mullaghmore (Ireland) and, in particular, to those documents relating to the quetion as to whether structural funds could be used for that project.
THE COURT hereby

1. Annuls the decision of the Commission of 2 February 1995 refusing the applicant access to Commission documents relating to the examination of a project to build an interpretative centre at Mullaghmore (Ireland);
2. Orders the Commission to pay the costs of the applicant;
3. Orders the Kingdom of Sweden, the French Republic and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to bear their own costs.
